statement: Today is a Thursday. What day of the week will it be $5^{2026}$ days from today?

choices.misconception: I found that 2026 leaves remainder 4 on division by 6 and moved forward 4 days, instead of working out the remainder of $5^4$ on division by 7.
I used the last digit of $5^{2026}$, which is 5, and moved forward 5 days, but the week has 7 days, not 10.
I divided the exponent 2026 by 7, got remainder 3 and used $5^3 = 125$, which leaves 6, but the powers of 5 repeat every 6 steps on division by 7, not every 7.
I found the remainder 2 correctly but counted today as the first day, so I moved forward only one day.

hints: Only the remainder of $5^{2026}$ on division by 7 matters.
Find the remainders of $5, 5^2, 5^3, \dots$ on division by 7 until they repeat. The length of the cycle tells you which small power behaves like $5^{2026}$.
The remainders are 5, 4, 6, 2, 3, 1 and then repeat every 6. Since 2026 leaves remainder 4 on division by 6, use the 4th one.

solutions.reliable: Days of the week repeat every 7, so we need the remainder of $5^{2026}$ on division by 7. The powers of 5 leave remainders 5, 4, 6, 2, 3, 1 and then repeat with period 6 (each is 5 times the one before, reduced). Since $2026 = 6 \times 337 + 4$, $5^{2026}$ leaves the same remainder as $5^4 = 625 = 7 \times 89 + 2$, namely 2. Two days after Thursday is Saturday. The transferable idea: for huge powers, find the cycle of remainders and reduce the exponent by the cycle length.
solutions.elegant: $5^3 = 125 = 126 - 1$ is one less than a multiple of 7, so $5^6$ is one more than a multiple of 7. Then $5^{2026} = (5^6)^{337} \times 5^3 \times 5$ behaves like $1 \times (-1) \times 5 = -5$, which is 2 more than a multiple of 7.

whyOnTest: Calendar questions are remainder questions in disguise, and huge powers are tamed by the repeating cycle of remainders.
